title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
authors: Ison HE, Clarke SL, Knowles JW
funder: No funding statement in the chapter. Acknowledgments: The FH Foundation, AHA, NIH, Doris Duke Foundation.
authorConflicts: No conflict-of-interest statement in the chapter. Author notes: Knowles is volunteer Chief Medical Advisor of the FH Foundation, a patient-led research and advocacy organisation; his research is funded through the NIH, a Doris Duke Foundation grant and, in part, the AHA.
result: Expert-authored, peer-reviewed chapter, first posted 2 January 2014, comprehensive update 7 July 2022, revised 30 January 2025. APOB-, LDLR- and PCSK9-related familial hypercholesterolaemia is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. Pathogenic LDLR variants account for more than 50% of FH; of pathogenic LDLR variants, about 85% are identified by sequence analysis, which detects missense, nonsense and splice-site variants and small intragenic deletions/insertions, and about 15% by gene-targeted deletion/duplication analysis, which detects intragenic deletions or duplications. Heterozygous LDLR-related FH: LDL cholesterol often above 190 mg/dL. Biallelic LDLR pathogenic variants: untreated adults often have LDL cholesterol above 500 mg/dL (above 13 mmol/L), and most develop severe coronary artery disease by their mid-20s.
